base_time_policy.content:
## Formal basis

Virtual Compute — For a service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request. For a service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than outage claim filing period after the official incident closes. For a newly filed claim, frozen handling time is its request notice time; the request is recorded immediately. Later review and credit use that recorded request notice time to evaluate the same boundary, so a timely request does not expire while awaiting review. Add outage claim filing period UTC calendar dates to official incident closing time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods. Equality at the deadline qualifies; a later claim is rejected without a credit. The provider incident must be completed, with cause outside outage exclusions. Availability at or above sla target percent gives no credit. Below the target choose the first descending sla credit bands entry whose minimum is no greater than the recorded availability percent. Multiply the original source charge pretax net amount by that fraction; subtract the the pretax service-credit total component of prior credits for that exact source, and cap total service credits at cumulative outage credit cap fraction of that original net amount. Floor the additional credit at zero and round with monetary decimal precision and rounding convention. Apply the original tax component proportionately. A review writes its nonnegative approved result; a financial credit writes the negative approved amount only after that approved review exists. This service-credit branch applies only to source subtype service credit; the invoice correction basis applies only to source subtype correction. Excluded incidents, ineligible reviews and zero remaining entitlement result in no financial write. A request for consequential-loss compensation is not covered. A service-credit financial posting requires an approved review with decision eligible and positive approved credit amount; the request and incident alone cannot authorize the financial posting.

## Evidence — claim deadline

For request, For a service credit request being filed, the outage claim is filed no later than outage claim filing period after the official incident closes. Before this action, authoritative system records establish the condition using evidence event reference, official incident closing time, request notice time. Those records correlate to the current action by evidence event reference.

## Calendar boundary

Add outage claim filing period UTC calendar dates to official incident closing time, preserving its time of day; calendar dates are counted without substituting business days or elapsed-hour periods. The anchor is official incident closing time, recording the official incident closes. The duration is outage claim filing period. Equality at the boundary qualifies.

## Hypothetical case

Hypothetically, a claim filed at the incident-based deadline meets the time condition; a claim filed later is rejected without a credit. Later review uses the recorded notice time, so a timely filing remains timely.

## Evidence — approved service credit

For credit, For a service credit financial posting, an approved review has decision eligible and positive approved credit amount for the exact source charge; this gate does not constrain filing or reviewing the request. Before this action, authoritative system records establish the condition using evidence event reference, original source reference, status, decision, approved credit amount. Those records correlate to the current action by original source reference.

## Basis — combined corrected amount corrected amount

Virtual Compute snapshot debit — Round the remote component half-up to two USD decimals and add it to the already rounded reviewed local snapshot subtotal to obtain the final corrected net corrected amount; the local reduction does not apply to this remote component.

## Basis Q&A

**What is the judgement for snapshot debit — combined corrected amount?**

Round the remote component half-up to two USD decimals and add it to the already rounded reviewed local snapshot subtotal to obtain the final corrected net corrected amount; the local reduction does not apply to this remote component.

## Hypothetical case

Hypothetically, the rounded local subtotal is 12.34 USD and the unrounded remote amount is 0.125 USD. Round the remote amount to 0.13 USD, then add it to obtain 12.47 USD. No local reduction acts on the remote amount.
